sbsistemas.what: I consolidated my professional foundation in front-end development, building applications with a focus on usability, maintainability, typing, reusable components, and engineering best practices.
impact: Developed front-end applications with React, Electron, TypeScript, and JavaScript
Implemented reusable components and interface standards
Applied maintainability, testing, and code quality practices

smarten.what: I worked as a Front-end Tech Lead in SaaS products, leading developers, defining quality standards, evolving interface architecture, and connecting technical decisions to product delivery.
impact: Technically led a team of developers
Created and maintained a Design System adopted across multiple products
Implemented CI/CD, monitoring, and quality standards

luizalabs.what: I worked at Luizalabs, Magalu's technology unit, developing web and mobile applications for physical store operations, REST APIs, and backend solutions for a high-scale national retail environment.
impact: Developed solutions used in inventory and logistics operations across 1,000+ stores
Contributed to the daily workflow of 1,000+ stock clerks in corporate applications
Maintained REST APIs, integrations, and micro frontends with React, React Native, Node.js, and TypeScript

lemon.period: July 2026 - present · AI team, inside Finance
lemon.what: On Lemon's AI team, I work from inside a business area: I live the Finance operation, find the manual work and decide what becomes product. Since August, I have shipped six internal products to production, from the screen to the database and the AWS infrastructure.
impact: Six finance products in three months: bank reconciliation, payment batches, suppliers, invoices and debit notes
Each one end to end: React front end, Fastify API with PostgreSQL and the infrastructure written as code with Pulumi
On AWS: containers on ECS Fargate, database on Aurora (RDS), events with EventBridge and SQS, secrets in Secrets Manager, delivery through API Gateway and CloudFront
A fast delivery pace, with AI agents in the loop and critical review before anything goes live

klick.name: Klick
klick.tagline: An offline-first speedcubing timer for all 13 WCA events.
klick.heroAlt: Klick's timer on desktop, with the scramble and the session averages

pain.title: The history that vanished.
pain.body: In the research before Klick v2, the most repeated story was from people who lost months to three years of times: cleared browser data, a new phone, an app that didn't keep them properly.
pain.caption: paraphrased from real reports on cubing forums, from the Klick v2 research

decisions.title: What came first.
items: Times live on the device (IndexedDB) and the app works offline after the first visit.
Automatic local backups every 50 solves and once a day, with a 30-day trash.
An optional, passwordless account (email code or passkey) to sync and keep cloud copies.
All 13 WCA events with official scrambles, and csTimer import for people coming from it.

product.title: Live, on desktop and phone.
product.body: An installable PWA with stats, goals, a training calendar, a learning trail with a 3D cube and challenge links, no account needed.

gallery: Klick's stats tab with records, averages, goals and the training calendar

grimory.name: Grimory
grimory.tagline: A D&D 5e table in Portuguese, from character to session.
grimory.heroAlt: Grimory's compendium open on the Longsword

pain.title: The sheet in the middle of the session.
pain.body: Players open their sheet on the phone mid-game: one hand, quick glances, numbers to roll and rules to check without leaving the sheet. The DM runs combat from a laptop.

decisions.title: The AI proposes, the rules decide.
items: Describe a concept and the AI proposes a complete, justified sheet that opens in the builder for review.
The rules engine validates everything: an invalid option never shows up.
Each table picks the 2014 or the 2024 rules, and every screen respects that choice.
Only distributable content: SRD 5.1 and 5.2 under CC-BY-4.0, with the source on every rule.

product.title: Used by his group's table.
product.body: A sheet that knows the rules, a translated compendium with the table's homebrew, a session diary and the Chama-guia, the familiar that gives the AI a face.

gallery: Grimory's home with the sample table's next session
A character's inventory on a phone, with the Chama-guia in the corner

build.title: Built with agents, reviewed by me.
build.body: React and Vite for the app, Astro for the public page and Cloudflare Workers for the table API and the AI (Claude through the Anthropic API). Today it is a prototype, with a closed beta in the cloud.
